A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same VITAL benchmark. The main text, figures, tables, and Appendices A–D support reliable comparison, including matching relocated analyses and renumbered displays.

before.justification: V1 reports original benchmarking of eight LLMs, human relevance and response evaluations, dataset analyses, and experiments with community models and agents.

after.justification: V2 retains these original empirical results and additionally reports inference times in Appendix Table 14.

M1.justification: The dataset filtering procedure and alignment methods are retained. The GPT-4o-selected, role-assigned Mistral-7B agents already appear in v1; their relocation does not introduce a new method.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same English healthcare situations, survey questions, polls, and moral scenarios across Overton, Steerable, and Distributional modes. Table 2 retains the same 18,846 samples.

E2.justification: Vanilla, prompting, MoE, and ModPlural remain compared across the same eight main LLMs. Cultural-community and mental-llama2-7b comparisons are also retained. The new timing table uses existing comparators.

E3.justification: The new inference-time evaluation assumes parallel community-model calls, averaging 6.11 seconds, followed by main-model processing (v2 Table 14). Existing benchmark metrics and sampling remain unchanged. Section 4.4 largely relocates settings already disclosed in v1 Appendix B.

E4.justification: V2 adds a computational-cost comparison through the Overton inference-time table. Sentence-length bias, entropy, specialised-model substitutions, agent-count sensitivity, and qualitative case studies were already examined in v1 and are retained.

E5.justification: There are no added run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, or significance tests. Human annotation agreement remains Fleiss’ kappa 0.49. The new averages across models summarise results rather than provide uncertainty estimates.

E6.justification: Matched per-model benchmark scores and plotted results are unchanged. V2 adds inference times and average columns in Tables 7 and 15–18. Some new averages are inconsistent with their component scores: Table 18 reports 0.349 for aligned ModPlural, whereas its eight displayed values average approximately 0.324.

T1.justification: Pluralistic-mode definitions and distributional targets in Appendix A.2 are unchanged. Neither version introduces additional formal assumptions, derivations, theorems, or proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list, and conclusion retain the same claims: VITAL provides a healthcare-specific pluralistic-alignment benchmark, and existing alignment techniques inadequately represent diverse healthcare perspectives.

C2.justification: Interpretations concerning incomplete community-message coverage, sentence-length bias, entropy reduction, and specialised models are retained. Limitations concerning English-only coverage and incomplete representation of perspectives also remain unchanged.

D1.justification: V2 replaces the future-release promise with stated code/data availability and a repository link. It specifies the binary health-relevance annotation question and the response-preference question permitting ties, and documents timing assumptions. Hardware and community-model details mostly move from Appendix B into Section 4.4.

R1.justification: The cited works and related-work positioning are unchanged after accounting for pagination. The agent-related citations and healthcare-specific novelty argument were already present in v1.

P1.justification: V2 introduces an Experimental Settings subsection using existing appendix material, places the agent analysis before the entropy analysis, and makes limited wording clarifications. The broader narrative and section structure remain substantially intact.

P2.justification: V2 adds timing Table 14 and average columns to existing result tables. Existing plots and tables are redistributed: v1 Figure 2 becomes v2 Figure 4, while v1 Figures 3–4 become v2 Figures 2–3. Captions and appendix numbering are adjusted without replacing the retained visual evidence.

improvement.justification: V2 improves access information and annotation transparency and adds useful timing evidence. However, several new averages introduce numerical errors. In Table 16, reported aligned MoE and ModPlural averages of 45.98 and 45.60 reverse the ordering obtained from their unchanged component scores, approximately 45.48 and 45.66. With the core study unchanged, these practical gains and losses in numerical reliability do not establish a clear net quality improvement or deterioration.
